tagline: Down the lake's east shore to the town the fire halved.
intro: Idaho 97 leaves Interstate 90 at the east end of Wolf Lodge Bay and runs south along the east shore of Lake Coeur d'Alene, a winding two-lane road at the foot of the national forest hills, with few places to pass. Bald eagles and nesting osprey live along this shore.

The lake was made by the Missoula Floods at the end of the last Ice Age. Past Harrison the road crosses the Coeur d'Alene River and heads southeast through the Coeur d'Alene Reservation to meet Idaho 3.
season: Visit Idaho says any time of year, with eagle watching at its peak in December and January.

moments.title: Wolf Lodge Bay
moments.text: In December and January the eagle watching is at its peak along the shore between Wolf Lodge Bay and Beauty Bay.

moments.title: Mineral Ridge Trail
moments.text: At Beauty Bay a 3.3-mile interpretive trail runs through ponderosa pine and Douglas fir, with views out over the lake and stations on the area's plants and animals.

moments.title: Harrison
moments.text: Harrison was once the largest city on the lake, until a 1917 fire at the Grant Lumber Company burned about half the town, much of which was never rebuilt.
